# A tab dragged out of a group is restored into its source header, leaving two active tabs

## Context

Reported by @tobiu 2026-09-01 against the Workstation on `dev@96987351df`, with a screenshot and — decisively — the mechanism: *"look at the 2 active tabs => it is in fact the header i dragged left, getting restored."*

**The measured mechanism — this replaces an earlier claim in this body that the source keeps a real, restored button. It does not.**

The App Worker moves the component correctly: `getTabButtons()` on the SOURCE toolbar no longer lists the dragged item. What survives is the item's **old DOM node**, never removed. So one element id — `neo-tab-header-button-3` in the captured run — renders under **two** headers at once, and the stale node keeps the `pressed` class it left with. Nothing is restored, and there is no second component; the document holds a duplicate id.

Evidence, joined by bar id rather than list position:

```
bar toolbar-7 (new)     DOM ["Priority Alert Observatory"]                      engine tabs 1
bar toolbar-3 (source)  DOM ["Resident Activity Timeline",
                             "Priority Alert Observatory"]                      engine tabs 11
node ids in MORE THAN ONE bar: [{id: neo-tab-header-button-3, bars: [toolbar-7, toolbar-3]}]
```

The `11` is **not** an accumulation and not part of the defect: one rendered button plus ten legitimately collapsed catalog items (`hidden: true, mounted: false, removeDom: true`). The dragged item is not among them.

So the fix belongs in **the projection delta that moves a retained button between owners** — not in the sort zone's restore path, and not in the dock model, both of which behave correctly.

**Live latest-open sweep** at 2026-09-01T13:35:45Z: 12 newest open issues checked plus a targeted search on drag/restore/pressed/duplicate. Nearest neighbours are #16499 (*"Re-entry paints the pane in both embodiments"*, **closed**, about window embodiments rather than a within-window source header) and #17889 (pointer-event sensor migration, unrelated). No equivalent open issue.

## Reproduction

1. Open `apps/workstation`.
2. Drag **Priority Alert Observatory** out of its group — the group also holds *Resident Activity Timeline* — leftwards over the 100k grid.
3. Dock it as its own pane.

**Observed:** the new pane renders correctly. The *source* header now shows **both** `Resident Activity Timeline` and `Priority Alert Observatory`, each with an active underline.

**Expected:** the source header shows only the tabs it still owns.

## It is a regression, and the first bad commit is isolated

@tobiu suspected a regression and was right. Bisected against a **deterministic** reproduction (see below), 3 runs per probe:

| commit | date | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `478a9fafb8` before the DockLayouts anatomy rewrite | 08-29 | **3/3 pass** |
| `e9f10ba17e` the anatomy rewrite itself (#17841) | 08-29 | **3/3 pass** |
| `36332ff3f5` dock workspace tab drag boundary (#17926) | 08-30 | **3/3 pass** |
| `9954179bb7` inline + standalone chrome variants (#17950) | 08-31 | **3/3 pass** |
| **`14d1024f7a` project overflow into header actions (#17951 / #17960)** | **08-31** | **3/3 FAIL** |
| `937feac74e` · `8cfa78702b` · `origin/dev` | 08-31 → 09-01 | 3/3 FAIL |

`14d1024f7a` is the **immediate child** of the last good commit — `git log 9954179bb7..14d1024f7a` lists exactly one commit — so the boundary needs no further narrowing.

Two candidate mechanisms were ruled in/out at that boundary rather than assumed:

- **Not the drag/overflow handshake.** `whenProjectionIdle` / `onSortSnapshotReady` / `sortSnapshotPending` appear 6 times in the tab SortZone at *both* the last-good and first-bad commits. That coupling predates the regression.
- **The action-contribution surface is what arrived.** #17951 added `addActionContribution`, `bindActionItems` and `isToolbarActionContribution` to `src/toolbar/Base.mjs`, and `addActionContribution` **inserts an item into the same `owner.items` collection the sort math indexes into** (`startIndex`, `currentIndex`, `moveTo(fromIndex, toIndex)`). `tab/header/toolbar/SortZone#moveTo` already remaps item indexes to tab indexes to survive interleaved action items, which shows the hazard was anticipated there — but `me.dragComponent` is restored by reference, on a different path.

That is the area, not yet the line. The line-level cause is the next step and is **not** claimed here.

## The Architectural Reality

**The `container/SortZone.mjs` visibility-restore suspect below is RETIRED, not merely demoted.** The engine's source-bar tab set does not contain the dragged item, so nothing restored it into that collection and no visibility toggle explains a duplicate DOM id. That block also last changed at `7de06abd13` (#8156) and is unchanged across the regression boundary. It is recorded here so the path is not re-walked.

A second retraction: an earlier revision claimed this was *"not the doubled-subtree failure mode"* on the grounds that duplicate ids were empty. That instrument was scoped **within** one bar while the duplication is **across** two, so it answered a narrower question than the one asked. This defect is in the same duplicate-id family as #17980, reached by a different route — a cross-zone move rather than a bar write racing a reconcile.

`src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:590-595`, in the drag-end path:

```javascript
// Restore visibility of the dragged component (it's not in sortableItems if placeholder is used)
if (me.dragComponent) {
    let style = me.dragComponent.wrapperStyle || {};
    style.visibility = null;
    me.dragComponent.wrapperStyle = style;
}
```

The dragged tab button is hidden for the duration of the gesture and this restores it **unconditionally**. For the within-toolbar reorder the base class is written for, that is exactly right — the button never left. For a dock cross-zone move it is not: the item has been re-homed to another node, and the source's button is a component that should be retiring, not becoming visible again.

`Neo.dashboard.dock.interaction.TabSortZone#processDragEnd` (`src/dashboard/dock/interaction/TabSortZone.mjs:1136`) handles the cross-zone and tear-out terminals and calls into the base drag-end, but nothing in the path above distinguishes "the item stayed and was reordered" from "the item was re-homed" for the purposes of that visibility restore.

**Why the existing witness never caught it.** `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationDockSplitChromeNL.spec.mjs` already records `pressedCount` and `tabTexts` per container and deliberately leaves `pressedCount` unasserted, documented there as belonging to "the orphaned-DOM class". Its cue commits `edge-bottom` on `scale-tabs`, and on that path every container reports `pressedCount: 1` — so the arm is honest but its gesture does not reach this. The operator's gesture does.

## The Fix

Not prescribed — the reachability question comes first. Candidate shapes, in the order I would test them:

1. **Scope the visibility restore to the reorder case.** The base restores because it hid the component; if the terminal re-homed the item, the source's button is not the base's to un-hide. This keeps the change in the dock subclass rather than mutating shared drag semantics.
2. **Retire the source button at the cross-zone terminal**, so there is nothing left for a later restore to reveal.

Option 1 is smaller and does not touch the within-toolbar contract every non-dock consumer relies on; option 2 is right if the button is genuinely leaking rather than merely being re-shown.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Dragging an item out of a multi-tab group to a new dock node leaves the **source** container rendering exactly the tabs it still owns — asserted on rendered chrome, cross-referenced against the committed document so a model/projection disagreement cannot pass.
- [ ] No tab text appears in two containers at once, and no container reports more than one `pressed` tab, for the **operator's** gesture specifically.
- [ ] The arm reds before the fix. A `pressedCount` assertion that passes on unfixed source does not count — and note the existing split-chrome arm passes today, so a new gesture is required rather than a new assertion on the old one.
- [ ] The within-toolbar reorder is unchanged: dragging a tab to a new index inside one header still restores its button visible, and an arm pins that so the fix cannot be written as "never restore".
- [ ] `WorkstationDockSplitChromeNL.spec.mjs`'s `pressedCount` forensic note is updated — once this is fixed, the comment explaining why it is unasserted is stale, and the assertion may become enforceable there.
- [ ] The reachability question is answered in the diff's comments: whether the restore fires on the re-homed component or a distinct leaked one, with the evidence that settled it.
